guard: a successor manager completes a crashed predecessor's frozen registration gate on boot only when the freeze-holder is affirmatively gone under a complete CONNZ sweep; live and unestablishable stay loud refusals
why: NO BUILD IN `command`. The suite imports Manager relatively (`../src/manager.js`), so tsx
loads manager.ts itself and a mutation on it is live with no `dist` in the path. `@cotal-ai/core`
is already built for the broker/auth helpers; the boot heal lives in manager.ts, which is the
file these mutations edit. If that were wrong, mutation 1 would come back SURVIVED.
MUTATION 1 IS THE DEFECT VERBATIM: skip the boot heal, so a frozen registration gate still
blocks the successor with SPEC 13.8. It must kill the dead-holder success cell.
MUTATION 2 IS ASSUME-DEAD AT THE BOOT SEAM: the liveness probe always returns gone, so a live
holder is no longer refused as `holder-alive`. Eviction may still fail closed later; the named
cell is the admit condition, not the later barrier.
MUTATION 6 IS THE SILENT-DAMAGE REGRESSION: restore the old `raced` copy, which reported only
that the reopen did not land. Refusing is necessary but not sufficient — `raced` is the one
refusal thrown AFTER revoke and eviction, so a message that reads as a no-op sends an operator
to retry while a healthy race winner sits revoked and disconnected.
MUTATION 7 IS THE DEAD-SAFETY-NET REGRESSION: reword the lease refusal so the smoke's prose
fallback can no longer match it. The class-based arm still names the condition, so the primary
cell stays green — only the cell that re-runs the mapper on the class-stripped message goes red.
That is the point: this coupling broke once already and nothing reported it.
NOT GRADED HERE: the CLI `cotal reconcile-gate` path. Its dedicated smoke has strong real-broker
coverage but no mutation config. This file grades the successor BOOT and the shared reply mapper
through the exact boundaries the automatic repair depends on.

mutations.name: the defect restored: boot does not complete a frozen registration gate
mutations.replace: if (false && auth) await this.healFrozenRegistrationGate(authKv, iid, auth);
mutations.expectRed: DEAD HOLDER: successor start SUCCEEDS without `cotal reconcile-gate` (boot self-heal)
mutations.cell: DEAD HOLDER: successor start SUCCEEDS without `cotal reconcile-gate` (boot self-heal)
mutations.note: The shipped skip. A successor seeing a frozen registration gate still hits SPEC 13.8 and cannot register until an operator runs reconcile-gate.

mutations.name: assume-dead: boot treats every freeze-holder as gone, so a live holder is no longer refused by name
mutations.find: probeHolder: makeManagerHolderLivenessProbe({ space: this.space, servers, auth, log }),
mutations.replace: probeHolder: async () => ({ state: "gone", detail: "assumed gone; sweepComplete not consulted" }),
mutations.expectRed: LIVE HOLDER: the refusal is named `holder-alive`
mutations.cell: LIVE HOLDER: the refusal is named `holder-alive`
mutations.note: The admit condition is gone AND sweepComplete=true. Forging a gone verdict at the boot seam is exactly the TTL-shaped failure two reviewers independently refused.

mutations.name: stale tenure: boot mutates after its own per-instance manager lease is lost
mutations.expectRed: LEASE LOST: the refusal is named `lease-not-held`
mutations.cell: LEASE LOST: the refusal is named `lease-not-held`
mutations.note: The liveness and eviction RPCs can exceed the manager-lease TTL. Automatic repair must re-prove its own fencing tenure after the oracle reply and around every mutating phase.

mutations.name: swallow raced: boot continues after revoke and eviction even though its final reopen CAS lost
mutations.expectRed: RACED REOPEN: the refusal is named `raced`
mutations.cell: RACED REOPEN: the refusal is named `raced`
mutations.note: A raced reopen happens after family revoke and verified eviction. Seeing the gate open does not make those side effects benign, so automatic boot must refuse rather than register onward.

mutations.name: contradictory oracle: incomplete sweep is allowed to authorize gone
mutations.note: The boot contract names gone AND sweepComplete=true as the admit condition. Deleting the contradiction guard must make the new boot-seam cell red.

mutations.name: silent damage: a raced reopen reports itself as a no-op after revoke and eviction already landed
mutations.find:
`the token-pinned reopen of ${key} lost its CAS — a newer barrier moved the gate while this repair ran. ` +
        `THE GATE WAS NOT REOPENED, BUT THIS REPAIR HAD ALREADY MUTATED STATE: ${revoked.length} credential(s) REVOKED` +
        `${revoked.length ? ` (${revoked.join(", ")})` : ""} and ${evicted.length} holder(s) VERIFY-EVICTED` +
        `${evicted.length ? ` (${evicted.join(", ")})` : ""}. ` +
        `Those side effects landed under a freeze the race winner now owns, so they may have revoked and ` +
        `disconnected a HEALTHY incarnation. Re-observe the gate AND the credential family before retrying, ` +
        `and expect the winner to need a restart if it was evicted mid-registration.`,
mutations.replace: `the token-pinned reopen of ${key} lost its CAS — a newer barrier moved the gate while this repair ran. Nothing was reopened; re-observe before retrying.`,
mutations.expectRed: RACED REOPEN: the refusal DISCLOSES the revoke/evict side effects that already landed
mutations.cell: RACED REOPEN: the refusal DISCLOSES the revoke/evict side effects that already landed
mutations.note: The shipped copy before this change. It is true about the reopen and false about the repair: revoke and verified eviction ran first. `raced` still refuses under this mutation, so the fail-closed cells stay green and only the disclosure cell reds — which is the whole claim.

mutations.name: dead safety net: the lease refusal's prose drifts out of the smoke's fallback mapper
mutations.find: `boot self-heal refuses at ${checkpoint}: manager instance ${this.managerInstanceId} does not hold its own liveness lease (${detail}). ` +
mutations.replace: `boot self-heal refuses at ${checkpoint}: manager instance ${this.managerInstanceId} cannot prove its fencing tenure (${detail}). ` +
mutations.expectRed: LEASE LOST: the prose fallback names it too (the safety net is not dead)
mutations.cell: LEASE LOST: the prose fallback names it too (the safety net is not dead)
mutations.note: Exactly the drift that had already happened: the mapper matched a phrase the thrower no longer wrote. The class-based cell stays green under this mutation, so only the class-stripped cell can catch it.
